telemetry.describe_status: State: Terminated (Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137), Restarts: 4

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The container exceeded its configured cgroup memory limit (512Mi) during bulk record processing. JVM max heap (-Xmx450m) plus JVM off-heap native memory (metaspace, thread stacks, direct buffers) surpassed the Linux cgroup threshold, prompting kernel SIGKILL (137).

key_evidence: Memory cgroup out of memory: Kill process

immediate_actions: kubectl scale deployment payment-processor --replicas=0 -n fintech-prod
Increase container memory limit to 2Gi and requests to 1Gi in deployment manifest
Set JVM ergonomics: -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError

title: Severe CPU Throttling under Constrained CFS Quotas Causing P99 Latency Spikes

telemetry.pod_logs:
2026-10-25T09:30:10.100Z stdout F [INFO] Web server running on port 8080 (Gunicorn workers=4)
2026-10-25T09:31:00.000Z stdout F [INFO] Influx traffic increase detected: 3,200 req/sec
2026-10-25T09:31:12.340Z stderr F [WARN] Event loop tick delay exceeded 3,450ms (expected <10ms)
2026-10-25T09:31:15.890Z stderr F [WARN] High CFS quota throttling: 89.4% of execution periods throttled (nr_throttled=447/500)
2026-10-25T09:31:18.210Z stderr F [ERROR] Worker process 14 heartbeat timeout; unhandled requests queued=2,180
2026-10-25T09:31:20.400Z stderr F [ERROR] Client downstream timeout: 504 Gateway Timeout on /v1/checkout/process
2026-10-25T09:31:25.010Z stderr F [WARN] Process CPU quota exhausted: 20ms assigned per 100ms CFS period consumed in 14ms
telemetry.k8s_events:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON       OBJECT                                  MESSAGE
2m          Normal    ScalingReplicaSet deployment/checkout-api                 Scaled up replica set checkout-api-68d77f864c to 6
1m          Warning   Unhealthy    pod/checkout-api-68d77f864c-8j9q1       Readiness probe warning: probe took 4.2s to respond (timeout 1s)
telemetry.describe_status: State: Running (Throttled: 89.4% CPU periods), P99 Latency: 4,800ms

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The container's CPU limit (200m = 20ms quota per 100ms CFS period) is severely undersized for a 4-worker web server handling 3,200 req/sec. The Linux Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) throttles execution for the remaining 80ms of each period, causing thread stall, event loop lag, and 504 gateway timeouts.

immediate_actions: Remove or substantially increase `resources.limits.cpu` in deployment spec (recommended: remove CPU limit and set CPU request to 2000m to avoid artificial CFS throttling)
Enable HorizontalPodAutoscaler based on container CPU utilization

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The worker node k8s-node-worker-pool-04 exhausted available host memory (<100Mi remaining), activating the Kubelet eviction manager. Because data-indexer had burstable QoS and high memory usage, Kubelet evicted it to prevent node-level kernel panic.

immediate_actions: Cordon and drain unneeded workloads from the affected node: kubectl cordon k8s-node-worker-pool-04
Inspect memory consumers on host: kubectl describe node k8s-node-worker-pool-04
Set Guaranteed QoS (`requests == limits`) on critical pods to protect them from Kubelet eviction ranking
Add node autoscaling or provision additional worker capacity

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The container runtime (containerd) became deadlocked or unresponsive on node k8s-worker-gpu-02, causing the Kubelet's Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG) to miss its health heartbeat threshold (>3 minutes). The Kubernetes Node Controller transitioned the node to NotReady.

key_evidence: Node k8s-worker-gpu-02 status is now: NodeNotReady
container runtime containerd did not respond

immediate_actions: Restart containerd and kubelet services on the affected host: sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
If node remains unresponsive, cordon and evict workloads: kubectl drain k8s-worker-gpu-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
Check kernel dmesg for I/O hangs or systemd dbus exhaustion

2026-10-25T11:40:15.120Z stderr F [WARN] DB connection pool saturated: 50/50 connections leased, 240 waiting callers
2026-10-25T11:40:20.000Z stderr F [WARN] Health check endpoint /ready performs deep SQL check 'SELECT 1' and timed out after 1,000ms
2026-10-25T11:40:21.050Z stderr F kubelet: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.3.42:8080/ready": context deadline exceeded
2026-10-25T11:40:25.100Z stderr F kubelet: Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503 Service Unavailable
2026-10-25T11:40:30.000Z stderr F kubelet: Container catalog-server failed liveness probe, will be restarted
telemetry.k8s_events:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON       OBJECT                                MESSAGE
2m          Warning   Unhealthy    pod/catalog-api-88df9674c-4xpp9       Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.3.42:8080/ready": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
1m          Warning   Unhealthy    pod/catalog-api-88df9674c-4xpp9       Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
50s         Normal    Killing      pod/catalog-api-88df9674c-4xpp9       Container catalog-server failed liveness probe, will be restarted

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The `/ready` and `/healthz` probe endpoints perform synchronous database queries. Under database connection pool saturation, health checks timed out beyond the 1-second `timeoutSeconds` setting. Kubelet removed the pod from endpoints, then killed the container via failed liveness probe.

immediate_actions: Decouple liveness/readiness probes from external database connectivity (return HTTP 200 based on process liveness only)
Increase `timeoutSeconds` from 1s to 5s and `periodSeconds` to 10s
Implement a `startupProbe` to handle slow application warmups
remediation.verification_command: kubectl describe pod catalog-api-88df9674c-4xpp9 -n store | grep -A 8 'Liveness:'

title: Unschedulable Pod Due to Excessive and Impossible Resource Requests

telemetry.pod_logs: (Pod has not started execution. No container stdout/stderr logs produced.)
telemetry.k8s_events:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON             OBJECT                                            MESSAGE
5m          Warning   FailedScheduling   pod/ml-inference-engine-7cc4b749f-x8m2q           0/16 nodes are available: 16 Insufficient cpu, 16 Insufficient memory. preemption: 0/16 nodes are available: 16 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.
2m          Warning   FailedScheduling   pod/ml-inference-engine-7cc4b749f-x8m2q           0/16 nodes are available: 16 Insufficient cpu, 16 Insufficient memory. preemption: 0/16 nodes are available: 16 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.
telemetry.describe_status: Status: Pending (Reason: Unschedulable - 0/16 nodes available: 16 Insufficient cpu)

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The pod specifies `resources.requests.cpu: 128` and `memory: 512Gi`. The largest available worker node in the cluster only possesses 32 vCPUs and 128Gi RAM. As a single pod cannot span multiple nodes, kube-scheduler cannot place the pod, leaving it perpetually in Pending state.

immediate_actions: Inspect cluster node allocatable capacity: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.status.allocatable.cpu,MEM:.status.allocatable.memory
Right-size `resources.requests.cpu` and `resources.requests.memory` in the deployment manifest to fit within worker node allocatable limits (e.g. cpu: 4, memory: 16Gi)
If 128 vCPUs is genuinely required, provision specialized high-core node groups with appropriate nodeSelectors/tolerations

title: Service Has No Endpoints Due to Label Selector Mismatch

telemetry.pod_logs:
2026-10-25T12:00:00.000Z stdout F [INFO] Nginx master process started
2026-10-25T12:00:01.000Z stdout F [INFO] Configuration reloaded successfully
2026-10-25T12:05:00.000Z stdout F (Zero ingress requests received by Nginx container over 5 minutes)
telemetry.k8s_events:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON       OBJECT                       MESSAGE
5m          Normal    Successful   deployment/frontend-web      Scaled up replica set frontend-web-74b6df54c to 3
3m          Warning   NoEndpoints  service/frontend-service     Service has 0 endpoints matching selector app=web-frontend
telemetry.describe_status: Endpoints: <none>, Selector: app=web-frontend, Pod Labels: app=frontend-web

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The Service `frontend-service` defines selector `app: web-frontend`, whereas the Deployment pod template defines label `app: frontend-web`. Because no pods match the selector, kube-proxy creates no iptables/IPVS routing rules and EndpointSlice contains 0 addresses, causing 503 / connection refused for all client traffic.

immediate_actions: Align the Service selector to match pod labels: kubectl patch service frontend-service -n production -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"frontend-web"}}}'
Verify EndpointSlice population: kubectl get endpoints frontend-service -n production

title: Service Routes Traffic to Unhealthy / Wrong Canary Pods via Overlapping Selector

telemetry.pod_logs:
2026-10-25T12:20:00.120Z stdout F [INFO] API Gateway Canary v2.9-beta starting
2026-10-25T12:20:05.400Z stderr F [ERROR] Missing Redis schema migration v29: table 'rate_limits_v2' does not exist
2026-10-25T12:20:06.100Z stderr F [ERROR] Responding HTTP 500 Internal Server Error to client request /api/v1/auth
2026-10-25T12:20:10.220Z stderr F [ERROR] Responding HTTP 500 Internal Server Error to client request /api/v1/orders
telemetry.k8s_events:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON       OBJECT                             MESSAGE
2m          Normal    Updated      endpoints/api-gateway              Updated endpoints with 4 addresses: 10.244.1.10, 10.244.1.11, 10.244.1.12, 10.244.2.99
1m          Warning   Unhealthy    pod/api-gateway-canary-88cf5-99zxc Readiness probe HTTP 500 on /healthz

ground_truth_rca.root_cause: The production Service `api-gateway` has an overly broad selector `app: api-gateway`. When an experimental canary deployment was created sharing `app: api-gateway` without selector isolation (`release: stable`), Kubernetes automatically registered the broken canary pod into the production Service endpoints pool, corrupting 25% of all live user traffic with HTTP 500 errors.

immediate_actions: Update Service selector to specifically target stable release: kubectl patch service api-gateway -n production -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api-gateway","release":"stable"}}}'
Alternatively, isolate canary deployment with distinct `app: api-gateway-canary` label
Configure readinessProbe on canary pods so failing pods are not added to endpoints before schema readiness
remediation.verification_command: kubectl get endpoints api-gateway -n production -o wide
